contracts.description: The prior Milestone 4 report remains INCOMPLETE until the release audit succeeds
Every Milestone 4.0R work package has a machine-readable contract with a real verification entry
Realm v5 adapter owns RealmRuntime and contains no reload, epoch, registry, root, or completion-buffer shadow state
Realm v5 A, B, C, and D fixtures compile from Nexa source and pass bytecode v4 round-trip and verification
Every Realm v5 event invokes its production RealmRuntime or RuntimeHost API
Realm inspection snapshots read all required fields from production runtime structures
Every Realm v5 shortest path replays against a fresh RealmRuntime with field-level snapshot equality
Every rejected Realm v5 event has a stable rejection class and leaves the production snapshot unchanged
All fifteen failure points are injected at production pre-commit boundaries
Failure injection supports once, Nth, always, disarm, clear, and per-point statistics
Failure differential uses RealmRuntime and verifies atomic failure plus activation and cleanup trap semantics
Failure artifacts are populated from RealmInspectionSnapshot and declare zero shadow state fields
Complex host arguments expose non-owning string, struct, enum, array, buffer, option, and result views
Generated Rust host input bindings use borrowed complex types
Generated call_runtime decodes every complex type directly without HostValue materialization
Complex host returns preflight once and encode directly into reserved VM heap slots
Production RealmRuntime always uses call_runtime and never materializing HostRegistry::call
The complete complex generated host input, return, and error matrix performs zero system allocations
Every source-backed CompileError carries its exact non-empty source span or whole-function span
Source-backed diagnostics never synthesize a zero-to-zero source location
All 34 stable diagnostic codes have real emission definitions
A real diagnostic fixture emits and validates every registered stable code
High-value runtime traps resolve every script frame and host boundary to original Nexa source
Snapshot storage is byte-backed, typed, layout-checked, and independent of i32
Generated typed snapshot codecs cover nested values and Combat stores a real EnemyView snapshot
Release audit binds the clean implementation commit and tree to generated JSON and Markdown evidence
